nodes.title: Notes
widgets_values: I use a NSFW Flux.2 Klein 9B distilled checkpoint as a GGUF, and an uncensored CLIP model as a GGUF. This can run on a 3070 Ti with 8GB of VRAM in 60-100 seconds. If you like different models, feel free to wire them up here.

nodes.title: Notes
widgets_values: I usually don't use LoRAs, but they're here if you want them.

nodes.title: Notes
widgets_values: Image Saver saves in a format where Civitai can successfully import the prompt - huge time saver.

nodes.title: Notes
widgets_values: I need to purge VRAM here. If you are blessed with more than 8GB of VRAM, feel free to disable this to save load times on future runs.

nodes.title: Notes
widgets_values: I have a separate Flux folder in my ComfyUI output folder, but you do you.

nodes.title: Notes
widgets_values: You can rename input slots for easy reference by right clicking on the dot and selecting Rename Slot.

nodes.title: Notes
widgets_values: I find 8 steps is the sweet spot for quality/time. 4 steps is suitable for drafts or experiments. Fun fact: Klein is not designed to be used with a CFG or denoise value, so those settings aren't actually doing anything in this workflow - they are simply here in case you want to plug in a different model that does.

nodes.title: End of Prompt
widgets_values: Highly detailed, cinematic lighting, photorealistic, 8k resolution.

nodes.title: Notes
widgets_values: I find this combination of prompts works 99% of the time, but feel free to experiment.

nodes.title: Notes
widgets_values: The prompt trails off at the end, because the character description will be injected here.

nodes.title: Notes
widgets_values: Note I am not using any of the built-in mask tools in Reference Latent+. The prompt is much better at handling that in my experience. I use a strength of 1.0 for the first image (scene) and 0.9 for the second (character), but feel free to experiment. (You need to expand Image 1 mask + timestep to see these settings).

nodes.title: Notes
widgets_values:
You can add as many face or character references as you like, and wire them up to Any Switch Select. Crop the image to show only the elements you want to use - if you only want to use the face and hair, crop it show only the face and hair.

In the String underneath each character, write a short description of the character traits you want to use - face, hair, clothes, etc. This will automatically be injected into the prompt when that character is selected.
